scope: Investigation only; no production changes, provider calls, or user Document writes
method: Existing log timestamps establish observed exchange intervals, not isolated CPU durations.
replay.mjs reuses the existing typing benchmark CDP harness, with a separate headless Chrome profile and blank page served through interception.
Actual native source modules load through the existing Vite dev server. API and external fetch calls are blocked; no service calls were attempted.

The eight-contribution Document is read from disk, copied into memory, and its latest saved XML response is replayed with freshly issued source aliases. Replay inserts a ninth contribution; it does not reconstruct the original pre-eighth-contribution state.
Mounted replay uses ReactiveTreeView, not the complete Dialectic application. These are isolated CPU measurements, not guaranteed user-visible latency or a Flint typing benchmark.
loadEditorMs and mountMs are fixture setup costs, excluded from exchange costs.

saveCaptureMs plus saveEncodeMs measures one native capture and encoding. fullSaveWithInMemoryAdapterMs measures ResourcePair.save with an immediately successful in-memory adapter, including its second capture/encoding for dirty comparison. It excludes filesystem/network persistence.

browser.json is the initial replay. browser-save.json adds the focused full-save measurement. The script reproduces the latter on the locally available fixture; it contains no copied conversation text.
continuity-store.json measures the existing compiled store using a temporary directory, which was removed afterward. No current session journal was changed.
storage-size.json uses compact JSON bytes for the existing native Document and summed embedded contribution diagnostic records; this is size evidence, not a measurement of their individual CPU cost.
No production performance correction has been implemented. No before/after improvement is claimed.
limits: Logs do not timestamp the final XML character becoming visible in the browser.
Body-to-outcome intervals include server/client work and scheduling; they are not XML conversion times.
Isolated replay costs and live log intervals must not be added together or treated as the same exchange.
